---
title: "16. Automatic Flowline selection"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{16. Automatic Flowline selection}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Flowline follows Hydro Modify in the Study workspace. Opening the tab uses the
selected Survey Event and Stream, reads the exact saved Hydro revision and its
current synthetic Stream Network candidate, and selects one raw Stream-level
path without asking the analyst to choose network heads or segments. Stream
definition already records that intent.

`flowline_review_server()` resolves the saved inputs through
`hydro_read()`, `stream_network_read()` and `stream_segments()`. The ordinary
`load_flowline_review()` adapter reads `stream-network.gpkg` and calls
`fluvgeo::select_stream_mainstem()`. The backend validates a one-outlet acyclic
directed tree, enumerates every complete head-to-outlet route and compares each
full terrain path with the retained NHDPlusV2 Stream geometry using discrete
Hausdorff distance. Among equivalent best reference matches it selects the
longest route; stable upstream-cell ordering resolves a remaining exact tie.
Reference geometry identifies the selected Stream but never supplies output
coordinates.

The result includes one downstream-to-upstream `sf` Flowline, the ordered source
`stream_line_id` rows and every candidate route with length, reference mismatch,
rank and selection flags. This raw result can enter the existing
`fluvgeo::flowline(flowline, reach_name, dem)` preparation contract. That function
continues to accept arbitrary browser-drawn lines for `{ohwm2}`; correctly defined
projected terrain lines now pass through its historical WGS84/Web Mercator CRS
repair unchanged.

The app map displays the selected raw path in gold, the complete synthetic
network in muted cyan and saved NHDPlusV2 evidence in dashed magenta over the
same viewport-stretched Hydro DEM and hillshade used for terrain review. The
summary reports the routes evaluated, source-line count, path length, reference
mismatch and next-best reference margin. This is a review-only result: no branch
choice, smoothing control, Reach split or candidate publication is implemented
in this slice. Missing or incompatible prerequisites fail with a route back to
Hydro Modify instead of inventing geometry.

| Data object / preparation asset | Operation | Storage and ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Saved Hydro DEM revision | `hydro_read()` | Existing Hydro-revision external GeoTIFF; read-only |
| Synthetic Stream Network revision | `stream_network_read()` | Existing Hydro-revision-local `stream-network.gpkg`; read-only |
| Retained NHDPlusV2 Stream evidence | `stream_segments()` | Hash-linked Stream selection/piece GeoPackage; read-only reference evidence |
| Automatically selected raw Stream path | `select_stream_mainstem()` | Transient `sf` result with ordered source-line and candidate-score evidence; not yet a saved or governed Flowline |
| Viewport elevation/hillshade | `prepare_hydro_dem_view()` | Regenerable session display from the Hydro GeoTIFF; analytical terrain is unchanged |

On the saved Spencer Creek inputs, the current candidates contain 15, 16 and 15
complete paths. Selection took 1.38, 0.44 and 0.31 seconds respectively on the
development workstation. The selected route was also the longest complete route
for all three Streams. The mainstem and east tributary had next-best Hausdorff
margins of 447.8 and 475.9 metres. The west tributary's two best reference
distances tied, and the longer of those routes was selected as specified. These
measurements qualify the current review examples, not all terrain forms.

Verification routes are `test-flowline-review.R` in FG Studio and
`test_select_stream_mainstem.R` plus `test_flowline.R` in `{fluvgeo}`. The next
feature increment compares bounded smoothing methods on these same raw paths,
then divides the accepted continuous Stream path at ordered Reach-source
boundaries and publishes immutable local candidates.
